blocks.text: 1. Macro-Prudential Regulatory Architecture & Basel III Framework

blocks.content: The global financial architecture established under the Basel III accord (developed by the Basel Committee on Banking Supervision - BCBS) aims to enhance the banking sector's ability to absorb shocks arising from financial and economic stress. In India, the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) mandated a minimum Capital to Risk-Weighted Assets Ratio (CRAR) of 9.0%, which is higher than the international Basel III requirement of 8.0%.

blocks.context: Basel III global minimum is 8.00%; RBI imposes 100 bps additional buffer
Maintained in the form of CET1 capital, bringing effective minimum CRAR to 11.50%

blocks.title: Exam Trap: AT1 Bond Write-Down Triggers & Point of Non-Viability (PONV)
blocks.content: Additional Tier 1 (AT1) bonds can be fully written down or converted into equity by the RBI WITHOUT shareholder consent if the bank reaches a Point of Non-Viability (PONV).
blocks.trapDetails: AT1 bonds carry higher yields because they do not have fixed maturity dates and coupon payments can be cancelled by the issuer without declaring default.

blocks.text: 2.1 Quantitative Worked Example: Banking Treasury SGB Yield & Price Calculation

blocks.title: Worked Example: Valuation & Macaulay Duration of a 10% Semi-Annual Government Security
blocks.question: A Scheduled Commercial Bank holds a 3-year Government of India bond with a Face Value of ₹10,00,000, bearing a annual coupon rate of 10% paid semi-annually. If the current market yield (YTM) required by the market is 8% per annum (4% per half-year), calculate: (a) The current market price of the bond, (b) The exact semi-annual cash flow table, and (c) Whether the bond trades at a premium or discount.
given: Annual Coupon Rate = 10% (Semi-Annual Coupon C = ₹50,000 every 6 months)
Maturity (N) = 3 years (Total periods n = 6 semi-annual periods)
Market YTM (r) = 8% per annum (Semi-annual rate r_half = 4% = 0.04)
blocks.method: Step 1: Compute periodic coupon payments. Step 2: Discount each of the 6 periodic cash flows using the semi-annual YTM of 4%. Step 3: Discount the final face value principal at period 6. Step 4: Sum all discounted cash flows to arrive at exact market value.

steps.title: Calculate Semi-Annual Coupon Payment
steps.explanation: Coupon = Face Value × (Annual Coupon Rate / 2) = ₹10,00,000 × 5% = ₹50,000 every 6 months.

steps.title: Discount Coupon Stream (Annuity Present Value)
steps.explanation: Discount factor for semi-annual rate r = 4% across 6 periods: PV_coupons = ₹50,000 × [(1 - (1+0.04)^-6) / 0.04] = ₹50,000 × 5.242137 = ₹2,62,106.85.

steps.title: Sum Cash Flows to Determine Bond Market Price

blocks.answer: The market price of the bond is ₹10,52,421.38. Because the Coupon Rate (10%) exceeds the YTM (8%), the bond trades at a PREMIUM of ₹52,421.38 above face value.

blocks.text: 3. Resolution of Stressed Assets: SARFAESI vs IBC 2016 Framework

blocks.content: Non-Performing Assets (NPAs) are classified when interest or principal installment remains overdue for a period of more than 90 days in respect of a term loan. Special provisions apply for agricultural loans (2 crop seasons for short duration crops, 1 crop season for long duration crops).

blocks.caption: Asset Classification & Provisioning Norms prescribed by RBI
rows: Identified by internal auditor / RBI inspector as uncollectible

blocks.title: Evolution of Insolvency & Stressed Asset Resolution Laws in India

events.title: Enactment of SARFAESI Act, 2002
events.description: Empowered banks to enforce security interest without intervention of courts/tribunals.

events.title: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code (IBC) Enactment
events.description: Unified framework creating National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) and 180-day time-bound resolution (extendable to 270/330 days).

events.title: Pre-Packaged Insolvency Resolution Process (PPIRP)
events.description: Introduced under Section 54A of IBC specifically for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) with ₹10,00,000 threshold.
